operative_text.controlling:
10.45(1)  After hearing an appeal from an assessment officer’s
decision, the judge may, by order, do one or more of the following:
(a) confirm, vary or revoke the decision;
(b) revoke the decision and substitute a decision;
(c) revoke all or part of the decision and refer the matter back
to the same or another assessment officer;
(d) make any other order the judge considers appropriate.
(2)  If the amount of costs payable as originally assessed by the
assessment officer has been paid and, after payment, is reduced on
appeal, the judge hearing the appeal may order the return of the
excess by the party who has received it and the order may be
enforced as an order of the Court.

BOOK_A.title: Decision of the Judge
BOOK_A.commentary:
An appeal from an Assessment Ofﬁcer is on the record and gets deference because of the
Assessment Ofﬁcer’s experience and knowledge.⁶

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.648(3). It came from 1944 C. R.780, as amended by Alta. Reg.86/60. New R.10.45(2) was enacted by Alta. Reg.163/2010.

Paragraphs (1)(a)-(d) and (2) are complete.
BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.10-136 (line 7299) to p.10-137 (line 7317): title (line 7299), rule text (lines 7300-7311), Related Provisions (lines 7313-7314: '10.26 (appeal from review officer)'), the note (lines 7316-7317, one sentence: 'An appeal from an Assessment Officer is on the record and gets deference because of the Assessment Officer's experience and knowledge.', marker '6') and 2 footnotes in the p.10-136 block (lines 7327-7329): fn 5 (history: 'Quite similar to previous 1968 R.648(3). It came from 1944 C. R.780, as amended by Alta. Reg.86/60. New R.10.45(2) was enacted by Alta. Reg.163/2010.') and fn 6 ('Vizor v.383501, supra (¶'s 80 ff. )'); fns 1-4 of that block (lines 7320-7326) belong to the 10.44 note. Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.45 apart from the marker, the ligatures and the amendment bracket (see the text note). (1) Related Provisions '10.26 (appeal from review officer)' is a label for official 10.26 'Appeal to judge'; the counterpart of 10.45 is 10.27 'Decision of judge', which is not listed here (the same 10.26 label is printed under 10.44). (2) The note's sentence agrees with official 10.44(2) (an appeal on the record) and with the 10.44 note's fn 3; 'gets deference' is not in the rule and comes from Vizor v.383501 Alta. 2022 ABQB 5 (fn 6, ¶'s 80 ff.), whose full citation is fn 1 of the 10.44 note (line 7320), so the 'supra' points back correctly. (3) The history footnote's statement 'New R.10.45(2) was enacted by Alta. Reg.163/2010' agrees with the official history ('AR 124/2010 s10.45;163/2010'); the old-rule references (1968 R.648(3), 1944 C. R.780, Alta. Reg.86/60) were not checked against any old-rule text. No infra and no '(#_)'-type placeholder is used. Book B has no commentary for this rule, so nothing in this note is corroborated by Book B (Book B's 10.44 commentary quotes 'Rule 10.45(1)' from Singh v. Noce para 3: the appeal judge may confirm, vary or revoke all or part of the decision, substitute a different decision, refer the matter back, or make any other order, which agrees with 10.45(1)(a)-(d)).
